subject: Discrepancy in collection timestamps causing billing mismatch
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam@tallyline.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Billing question — two collections on same invoice?

Hi Kimberly,

We noticed invoice INV-9398 shows a remaining balance after two payments cleared on our bank side. Payments were initiated on 2026-12-03 (ACH) and 2026-12-04 (card charge); both show as processed in our ledger. I attached our payment report. Can you confirm receipt and tell us why the invoice still shows an outstanding balance?

Two oddities we saw: timestamps in your hosted portal show a \"collection\" event at 23:59 UTC and another at 00:00 UTC the next day — could that have caused duplication or misapplied credits? Also, the invoice shows a token overage for Nov -> Dec window that doesn't match our internal usage tallies.

We need this resolved before our month-end close. Appreciate a quick look.

Thanks,
Liam O'Neill
Head of Finance, TallyLine.ai
attachments: tallyline_payment_report.csv (csv)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam@tallyline.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 17:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Billing question — two collections on same invoice?

Hi Liam — thanks for the attachment, that helps.

Quick notes after a first pass:
- We see two collection events in our payments pipeline for INV-9398 as well: an ACH settlement at 2026-12-03T23:59:12Z and a card authorization that captured at 2026-12-04T00:00:07Z. Those are separate clearing events but should both map to the same invoice once reconciled.
- The more likely root cause for the "remaining balance" is an internal ledger timing mismatch between the gateway settlement record and the invoice-finalization job (runs at midnight UTC). If the settlement hits just before midnight and another capture just after, our reconciliation job can temporarily show a residual.

To be safe Ive asked Billing Ops to pull raw collection and settlement logs and our metering batch for the Nov 28 - Dec 4 window. Ben, can you take point on the logs? If we confirm a reconciliation race, we should issue a provisional credit and follow up with a permanent ledger adjustment.

Liam — we'll follow up with evidence and a proposed credit schedule within 48 hours.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:08:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Billing question — two collections on same invoice? 

Forwarding TallyLine thread. I pulled the collection traces and our metering run results for the Nov 28 - Dec 4 boundary. Summary below (high level):

- Gateway settlements:
  * ACH settlement tx 0x9f4a at 2026-12-03T23:59:12Z (cleared)
  * Card capture tx 0x9f82 at 2026-12-04T00:00:07Z (cleared)
- Reconciliation job: invoice-finalize.sh started 2026-12-04T00:00:00Z and processed invoice INV-9398 using the snapshot taken at 2026-12-04T00:00:00Z. The ACH settlement arrived ~48 seconds earlier and was included in the snapshot, but the card capture came in 7s after the job started; the job did not re-run for that invoice. Result: the invoice marked paid -> then immediately flipped to show a residual when the card capture posted to the ledger separately.
- Metering: our token aggregator for Nov 30 - Dec 1 windows shows an unusual overlap: some streaming sessions open before midnight ran into the new day and were double-allocated across two buckets due to an edge-case in the prefix-KV flush. That produced a ~0.4% overcount for TallyLine during that boundary window (~11k tokens on their tier).

Attachments: redwood_collection-log-20261206.zip contains the raw gateway events and invoice-finalize logs. I've also attached a quick proposed_credit_schedule.xlsx that contains (A) provisional credit for the 11k-token overcount and (B) a reconciliation credit to neutralize the transient residual caused by the timing race while we apply a durable fix.

Recommendation:
1) Issue provisional credit equal to the token overcount (11k tokens) converted at their rate and apply an immediate invoice adjustment so their AR shows zero.
2) Run a targeted re-reconcile of INV-9398 using the capture window 2026-12-03T23:58:00Z -> 2026-12-04T00:05:00Z and post a permanent ledger adjustment if the re-reconcile confirms duplication.
3) Postmortem: add a 2-minute buffer to invoice-finalize.sh snapshots and flag streaming session flushes that overlap UTC midnight to prevent double-bucket allocation.

Marissa / David — can you validate the numbers and confirm we can do (1) as a provisional step while engineering implements the postmortem fix?

Ben
Senior Billing Analyst
attachments: redwood_collection-log-20261206.zip, proposed_credit_schedule.xlsx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam@tallyline.ai>, accounts_payable <payments@tallyline.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Billing question — two collections on same invoice?

Hi Liam — looping back with a readout after our investigation. Sorry for the delay; we wanted to be confident before proposing a fix.

What we found
- There were two clearing events for INV-9398 (ACH + card) and a reconciliation race at midnight UTC which created a transient residual.
- Our metering batch incorrectly allocated ~11,000 tokens twice across the Nov 30 -> Dec 1 boundary due to a streaming-session flush edge-case. That produced an overage line on the invoice that did not belong to TallyLine.

Actions taken
1) We posted a provisional credit today that zeroes the outstanding balance on INV-9398. You should see it reflected in your portal immediately.
2) We will run the targeted re-reconcile (window: 2026-12-03T23:58:00Z - 2026-12-04T00:05:00Z) tomorrow and, if confirmed, post a permanent ledger adjustment and send you the audit file.
3) Engineering has scheduled a postmortem change to invoice-finalize.sh (add 2-minute snapshot buffer) and a fix to the KV flush so streaming sessions that straddle midnight are accounted correctly. Target deploy: 2026-12-20.

Next steps for you
- If you can send the bank confirmation for the two clearing events (we received the records, but your payment report helps cross-verify), attach in reply.
- We'll follow up with the permanent adjustment and an exported audit CSV.

Apologies again for the disruption. Were also prepared to offer a one-time goodwill credit of one additional month of their embedding tier if this caused material accounting pain — we can discuss that separately.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
